name: Carboxymethyl cellulose
description: Carboxymethyl cellulose ( CAS 9000-11-7 ), commonly sourced as CMC or cellulose gum ( E466 ), is a water-soluble cellulose derivative used across food, pharmaceutical, and industrial markets. It functions as a thickener, binder, and stabilizer. Its ability to control viscosity and retain water at low use levels makes it a high-volume ingredient in both aqueous formulations and dry-mix systems. In food manufacturing, CMC functions as a texture modifier and stabilizer in ice cream, bakery fillings, sauces, and low-fat dairy products. It provides essential mouthfeel and shelf stability. Pharmaceutical tablet production relies on CMC as a binder and disintegrant. Crosslinked carboxymethyl cellulose serves specifically as a superdisintegrant in various solid dosage forms for rapid release. Detergent and household cleaning formulations use cellulose gum as an anti-redeposition agent. This prevents loosened soil from re-adhering to fabric during the washing cycle for better results. In construction, CMC improves workability and water retention in tile adhesives, gypsum compounds, and cement-based mortars. It is supplied as a white to off-white powder in various viscosity grades. Food-grade material is available to FCC specifications. Pharmaceutical grades meet USP , BP , and Ph. Eur. standards to ensure the highest level of safety and compliance for manufacturers. Technical grades serve industrial applications in textiles, paper sizing, and drilling fluids.
